issues.legal_issue: The effect of a final statutory acquisition of immovable property on the possessory rights of a contractual or statutory tenant.
material_facts: The appellants conducted business as tenants in a building under a monthly tenancy.
The building was acquired under a statutory scheme for acquiring immovable property transferred for an apparent consideration below its fair market value in specified tax-evasion circumstances.
The appellants contended that their tenancy rights survived the acquisition and allowed them to remain in possession as tenants of the Central Government.

The statutory scheme provided for notice to occupants and interested persons, an opportunity to object and appeal, compensation for persons entitled to it, and delivery of possession after the acquisition order became final.
issues.conclusion: A tenant, whether contractual or protected as a statutory tenant, has no right to remain in possession after the acquisition order becomes final and must deliver possession to the competent authority. When possession is obtained, the property vests absolutely in the Central Government free from encumbrances; the tenant may have a claim to share in compensation, but tenancy rights do not continue against the Government.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 269D, 269E, 269F, 269G and 269H of the Income-tax Act, 1961, occupants and other interested persons receive notice and may object to an acquisition and pursue appeals. Sections 269-I(1), (2) and (4) require surrender of possession after the acquisition order becomes final and provide for absolute vesting free from encumbrances when possession is obtained. Sections 269J and 269K provide for compensation and its apportionment among persons entitled to it, while the proviso to section 269-I(4) permits enforcement of surviving encumbrances against persons other than the Central Government by a suit for damages. Section 269AB supports the conclusion that transactions conferring rights to take or retain possession fall within the scheme. Gian Devi Anand v. Jeevan Kumar and Damadilal v. Parashram, concerning tenant protections under Rent Acts, do not alter the result under this acquisition scheme. The Court also noted that Rent Acts ordinarily exclude property owned by the Central Government.

predicates.statutory_immovable_property_acquisition: The proceeding concerns statutory acquisition of immovable property following a transfer alleged to have understated its value in circumstances connected with tax evasion.
predicates.tenant_in_occupation: A person holds possession of the property as a contractual tenant or as a tenant protected against eviction by rent-control law.
predicates.acquisition_order_final: The acquisition order has become final after the available objection and appeal process.
predicates.tenant_must_surrender_and_cannot_continu: The tenant must surrender possession and cannot continue to occupy the property, and the Government obtains title free from encumbrances once it obtains possession.

issues.definition: When a tenant occupies property acquired under a statutory immovable-property acquisition process and the acquisition order becomes final, the tenant cannot remain in possession, and the Government takes title free from encumbrances when it obtains possession.
